title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-FAIRROUND-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-FAIRROUND-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `818fe7861`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-FAIRROUND-1

## Summary

Ported the teammate-delivered `fair-round-20261108` fix for responder starvation
in `runTeammateResponder` (`src/core/comms/imessage-teammate-worker.ts`).

Bug: the scan was `inbox.texts.slice(0, 256)` over an `at`-ordered (record-time)
inbox. A text that is re-recorded late — e.g. `recordTeammateText` failing in
`ingestIMessages` (`deferred` break, cursor not advanced, re-ingested next poll
with a fresh `at`) — lands at the tail of the at-order, behind every newer
text. Under sustained arrival pressure beyond 256 unanswered rows, the old
receipt stays outside the bounded window forever; new replyable messages
indefinitely defer it.

Fix (fair scan rounds): the responder now freezes a per-round upper rowid
(`scanCeiling`) in the receipt store and sweeps the frozen range in rowid order,
tracked by a persisted cursor (`scanAfter`), across as many passes as the
per-pass bounds (256 examined, 3 work items) take. Eligibility is by rowid —
the stable arrival order — so an `at`-late straggler keeps its arrival rank.
Arrivals past the frozen bound wait for the next round: a bounded deferral,
never starvation. The round completes by coverage (every in-range text visited
once), so permanently-pending texts (unapproved/leader) cannot deadlock it;
they are re-swept in the following round as before. Budget-breakers restore
the pre-message checkpoint so they keep their existing retry-next-pass cadence.
Sibling precedent: `imessage-findings-bridge.ts` already re-sorts `texts` by
rowid for its watermark scan for the same `at`-inversion reason.

Files changed (all left uncommitted for publish.sh):

- `src/core/comms/imessage-teammate-worker.ts` (+24/-5):
  `Store` gains optional `scanAfter`/`scanCeiling` (schema-validated when
  present); the loop head becomes the round open/sweep; the two
  `processed >= 3` breaks restore the checkpoint; post-loop persists
  `scanAfter` and clears `scanCeiling` when the sweep reaches `rangeEnd`.
- `test/imessage-teammate-worker.test.ts` (+24/-1): two regression tests —
  an `at`-inverted old receipt behind 261 newer texts is replied to, and a
  post-ceiling arrival is held exactly one round then processed — plus the
  `senderIdFor` import.

## Patch provenance / deviation note

`~/.ashlr-runs/imessage/patches/patch-fair-round-20261108.RAW.diff` is not
readable from this worktree sandbox (`~/.ashlr-runs` is seatbelt-denied for the
agent process; `request_scope` grant, the `read` tool, `osascript`, `mdfind`,
the `gh` CLI config, MCP servers, and the hub API all failed or lacked access).
The fix was therefore reconstructed manually from the job description
("freezes a scan-round upper rowid so new arrivals cannot indefinitely defer
old receipts", superseding the withdrawn fair-scan candidate) and verified
against the starvation mechanism in the current source. If a reviewer diffs
against the RAW artifact, expect different line shapes for the same semantics.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/imessage-teammate-worker.test.ts` —
  16/16 PASS (2 new + 14 existing).
- Same file re-run with `HEAD` worker restored: the 2 new tests FAIL (14
  pass) — confirms they pin the fixed behavior. New code re-restored after.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS (once,
  foreground): file selection PASS, `tsc --noEmit` PASS, web typecheck
  skipped (no `src/web-ui` change), realio lane lint PASS, verse sync-I/O lint
  PASS. eslint SKIP: `node_modules/eslint/lib/cli.js` absent in this worktree
  (no `npm ci` run); Merge Gate lints on CI.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run check:docs` — PASS (`errors: []`).

## Pass/fail counts

- Tests: 16 pass, 0 fail.
- verify-changed: all applicable phases PASS; eslint skipped (no node_modules).
- check:docs: 0 errors.

## Net LOC

`git diff --stat`: 2 files, +48/-6 (net +42).

## Limitations

- Literal patch artifact unreadable under this sandbox; the port is a
  semantics-faithful reconstruction (see provenance note).
- eslint not run locally (no `node_modules`); relies on Merge Gate lint.
- No commit/push performed; changes staged only in the worktree for
  publish.sh.
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-REDIRECT-FIX-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-REDIRECT-FIX-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `818fe7861`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-REDIRECT-FIX-1

REWORKS_PR: 4088

## Summary

Security fix for PR #4088 (FIXUP-CI-phantom-ci local-bench transport), against
reviewed helper blob `48d16febab1378f4db5b5ad601b81430eda7ec55` (the worktree's
`src/core/radar/local-bench.ts` at HEAD — verified byte-identical via
`git hash-object`).

**Bug:** the bench validates that its base URL is loopback before any fetch,
but `chatCompletion` used the fetch default `redirect: 'follow'`. A validated
loopback endpoint answering 307/308 had undici re-POST the synthetic bench
body (instruction + fixture input) to whatever origin `Location` named — a
second hop nothing re-validated. The "loopback-only" guarantee therefore
leaked the request body to an arbitrary origin.

**Fix:** `redirect: 'error'` on the transport's fetch init — the same option
every other security-sensitive transport in this tree already uses
(`telemetry-sink.ts` "Never forward the credential to a redirect target",
`provider-client.ts`, `local-inference-probe.ts`, `ollama-identity.ts`,
`model-manager.ts`, …). Any redirect reply now fails the call; `scoreSuite`
records it as a `transport` error, the existing failure path. A legitimate
local model server never redirects `/v1/chat/completions`.

Module header "THE ONE RULE" and the emitted report `notes[]` now state the
redirect refusal so the documented invariant matches the code.

## Changes

- `src/core/radar/local-bench.ts` (+7/−2): `redirect: 'error'` in
  `chatCompletion`; header + report-notes wording.
- `test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts` (new, 78 lines, **real-io lane**):
  two real loopback HTTP servers — the first replies 301/302/303/307/308 with
  `Location` pointing at the second. Asserts the case is scored
  `error: 'transport'`, `answered: null`, and that the second listener saw
  **zero requests and zero body bytes**. Registered in
  `test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs` per the lane guard.
- `test/radar-local-bench.test.ts` (+20, unit lane): pins the transport
  contract — every `fetchImpl` call carries `redirect: 'error'`.
- `test/fixtures/radar-local-bench/README.md` (+3/−2): offline-test command
  names both suites; security-model line mentions redirect refusal.

## Commands run

```
# Affected tests (hermetic runner, temp HOME)
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/radar-local-bench.test.ts test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts
# → 2 files passed |unit| + |real-io|, 23 tests passed, 0 failed

# Regression proof: fix reverted, new suite must fail
git stash -- src/core/radar/local-bench.ts
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts
# → 5/5 FAILED without the fix (body reached second listener; case scored as answered)
git stash pop

# Repo verification (AGENTS.md: automated workers run once, foreground)
HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs --force
# → PASS file selection / tsc --noEmit / realio lane lint / verse sync-I/O / verify dedupe
# → SKIP eslint: node_modules/eslint/lib/cli.js absent in this worktree's
#   partial install (Merge Gate lints on CI)

# Docs check
npm run check:docs
# → PASS, errors: []

# Registry/drift suites touched by the new test file
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/authority-codeowners-310b.test.ts test/realio-lane-guard-green.test.ts test/doc-facts.test.ts
# → authority-codeowners PASS, doc-facts PASS
# → realio-lane-guard-green FAIL — pre-existing base-branch drift: it flags
#   test/ecosystem-changelog-generator.test.ts and
#   test/verse-standby-python-contract-02somp1.test.ts, both UNCHANGED here.
#   Not caused by this diff (verify-changed's changed-files scope: PASS).
```

## Pass/fail counts

- `test/radar-local-bench.test.ts`: 18/18 pass (was 17 before)
- `test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts`: 5/5 pass (301, 302, 303, 307, 308)
- Regression confirmed: all 5 fail without the fix
- verify-changed: all PASS (eslint skipped — see above)
- check:docs: PASS
- 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change: `realio-lane-guard-green`
  (flags two files untouched by this diff)

## Net LOC

Tracked: +31/−4 across 4 files; new file `test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts`
+78. **Net +109/−4** (net +105 lines). No changes committed.

## Notes

- Boundary respected: no `git commit`/`push`, no `gh` writes — publish.sh owns
  publishing. All changes uncommitted in the worktree.
- Only `chatCompletion` performs network I/O in this module; no other fetch in
  the bench needed the option.
- Chose `redirect: 'error'` over `manual` + re-validation: the codebase's
  established convention for credential/body-bearing transports, and any
  redirect here is already a transport failure — there is no legitimate
  redirect target to re-validate for.
</details>

pending comms item, aggregating four local sources into one ranked list whose

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-EVALFLEET-1

## Summary

Fleet-level eval harness ("fleet IQ"): `phm fleet eval-report --json` scores
every merged PR in a window for post-merge durability and rolls the results up
by lane, tier, lane+tier and repo. Read-only analytics; nothing merges, routes,
requeues or releases credit.

- `src/core/fleet/eval-report.ts` (new, 969 LOC): folds
  `~/.ashlr-runs/metrics/jobs.jsonl` (enqueue/launch/finish/publish/outcome
  rows), repeatable gh-shaped merged-PR exports (`gh pr list --state merged
  --json url,number,title,mergedAt,mergeCommit,files,statusCheckRollup,commits,body`,
  JSON array or JSONL) and the signed post-merge observation ledger into
  `fleet.eval-report.v1`. Durability is the worst evidence across channels
  (deterministic `Revert "title"`/`Revert #N` > overlapping fix-file follow-up;
  ledger rows keyed by mergeCommit), `stable` requires the 72 h window elapsed
  AND the merge's own row in a covering gh export, otherwise `pending` /
  `unobserved`. Rates resolve over stable+adverse only; `ranked` sorts on the
  Wilson lower bound; CI block reports raw adverse rates by check state and
  job-finish failure plus a direction — never a significance claim.
- `src/cli/fleet-eval-report.ts` (new, 165 LOC): thin adapter — bounded file
  reads (16 MiB cap, ≤8 `--prs` files), `--jobs/--prs/--days/--until/
  --no-observations/--json`, dep injection for tests, exit 2 on bad args,
  exit 1 when no input source is readable.
- Registry regenerated (`'eval-report'` loader), `eval-report` added to fleet
  completions, docs in AGENTS.md + `docs/FLEET-VERBS.md`.

## Design notes / honesty stance

- Ledger-only merges (repo covered by export, PR absent from it) still earn
  deterministic revert detection via `Revert #N` refs, but are never `stable`.
- Merges with pending (non-concluded) checks report `checkState: unknown`,
  not `clean`.
- Publish/outcome rows without lane/tier borrow the producing job's latest
  routing row; attribution resolves post-fold so out-of-order rows still join.
- `ttm_s` prefers the ledger value; `mergeLead` falls back to mergedAt minus
  the job's first routing timestamp.
- Bodies/titles are parsed only for evidence matching — never echoed into the
  report.

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-WTJANITOR-1 (fleet wt-audit)

## Summary

Adds `phm fleet wt-audit` — a read-only audit of the job-worktree root
(`~/Projects/ashlrai/wt`, ~912 dirs on the host) — plus a `--reap-plan`
mode that lists only worktrees the existing sanctioned reapers could
already take. The command deletes nothing, publishes nothing and writes
no queue state.

- `src/core/fleet/wt-audit.ts` (new, 722 LOC): injected-reader audit core.
  - Pure parsers: attempt-aware `jobs.jsonl` ledger (a `launch` resets
    terminal evidence of the previous attempt; `rows` never resets, so it
    stays the orphan detector), `mergedUrlsFromLedger` (dispatchd's
    `_merged_urls` shape), `.publish` RESULT classifier matching
    `reap-one.sh`'s case statement, `ps` scan (reap-one.sh/publish.sh
    children = in-flight; launch.sh/worktree/prompt paths = alive, with
    dispatchd.py self-rows filtered), status.json kept/reaping lists, and
    `queue/keep.txt`.
  - `classifyEntry` rolls evidence into one state per worktree:
    invalid / excluded (hidden + `guardian-*`) / running (`.dispatched`,
    `.pid`, live process, or named anywhere in status.json — reap-one's
    quiet check) / reaping / publishing / held (keep.txt, status
    `kept_worktrees`, `~/.ashlr/kept-worktrees.json` pins, RESULT
    DENIED/ABORT/secret-shape/other) / archived (RESULT ARCHIVED — needs
    the archive path's salvage verification) / merged / open / ended /
    published / empty / finished / recorded / orphaned / unknown.
  - Reap eligibility: `via: 'reap-one'` (job `.base` + terminal evidence;
    reap-one.sh runs publish.sh then removes) or `'worktree-remove'`
    (merged outcome, or published/empty without the `.base` the reaper
    needs — the removal `fleet worktree-stale --apply` / `wt-reap --apply`
    already performs). `reapable` only when `via` survives every gate.
  - Fail-closed gates strip `via` from every candidate when any safety
    source is unread: jobs ledger, status.json, process table, pin file,
    runs-dir listing (can't see `.base`/`.publish`), keep.txt, or the
    `queue/run` listing (can't see markers). `presence` distinguishes a
    positively-absent file (empty evidence, healthy) from a present-but-
    unreadable one (degraded). A 180 s evidence-freshness grace mirrors
    dispatchd's launch grace. Orphan is claimed only when every source is
    readable and still shows no evidence.
  - Sizes via the shared `measureWorktreeBytes` under one 20 s budget;
    bounded reads refuse symlinks (`O_NOFOLLOW`) and cap files at 256 KB /
    ledger at 8 MB.
- `src/cli/fleet-wt-audit.ts` (new, 84 LOC): thin dispatcher —
  `--json` (sanitized via `sanitizePublicJson`, home paths shown as `~`),
  `--reap-plan`, `--no-size`, `--wt-dir`, `--runs-dir`;
  `ASHLR_WT_DIR`/`ASHLR_RUNS_DIR` env like `fleet kept-age`.
  Exit 0 ok, 1 when the worktree root can't be listed, 2 bad usage.
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` (+1 generated line, `wt-audit`).
- `docs/FLEET-VERBS.md` (+1 table row, per the file's sync convention).
- `test/fleet-wt-audit.test.ts` (new, 452 LOC, 27 tests): fully hermetic —
  injected fs/ledger/ps/pins/measurer, temp HOME; covers attempt reset,
  publish classes, ps/status/keep parsing, every protected state, degraded
  fail-closed gates, freshness grace, realpath `.base` aliases, CLI exits.

## Safety properties

- Read-only: no deletes, no publishes, no marker or queue writes. The plan
  is a candidate list for the sanctioned tools (reap-one.sh, worktree
  removal), never an executor — same posture as `fleet reap-marks`.
- Never plans: running, reaping, publishing, held, archived, fresh,
  non-terminal, evidence-less, or any worktree while a safety source is
  unread. A `.base` only counts when its recorded worktree path resolves

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-CI-CANDIDATE-1

## Summary

Merge-evaluated the teammate's CI test candidate (described at master `6778b16`
as: quota custody preserving Darwin/APFS positive coverage + adding Linux
fail-closed, volume polling against the real storage checker, staging-stop
asserting both settled and unattempted reports). The candidate artifact itself
is not fetchable locally — `6778b16` is an unrelated worktree-heal commit, no
branch or PR ref containing it survives in this clone, and `gh` is blocked in
this sandbox — so the described semantics were reconstructed faithfully against
current HEAD, keeping only pieces still applicable.

## Ported

1. **Quota custody — own-pid self-clock verification**
   `src/core/resources/quota-refresh-lease.ts`: `observedOwnerStart` now uses
   `currentProcessStartIdentity()` when `lock.pid === process.pid`, keeping
   `verifiedProcessStartIdentity` (kernel probe) for foreign owners. This
   mirrors the established `hasVerifiedLiveOwner` convention in
   `src/core/fleet/local-store-lock.ts` ("the writer's immutable start
   identity… other owners still require a native probe"). Security-equivalent:
   for our own pid the self-clock is the same quantity ps-lstart would report,
   and the lock's `startRef` was written from it. Foreign-pid verification is
   unchanged and still fails closed when the probe is denied (ps on darwin,
   `/proc` fallback on linux).

2. **Quota custody — Linux fail-closed + own-custody coverage**
   `test/resource-quota-refresh-lease.test.ts` (which already mocks
   `readNativeBootIdentity: () => null`, simulating a non-darwin host):
   - new positive test: `lease.identity()` verifies own custody from the
     process start clock without a native probe.
   - new `it.each([2,3,4,5])`: a staged custody-bound pending marker on a
     host with no boot identity refuses acquisition with
     `reconciliation-required` / `boot-identity-unavailable` and preserves the
     marker — the Linux fail-closed custody path.

3. **Volume polling — real storage checker on the actual host**
   `test/resource-volume-polling.test.ts`: new darwin-gated test that swaps the
   mocked `execFileSync` for the real implementation and runs the full bounded
   sysctl/df/diskutil/plutil chain (`prepareResourceNativeProfile` →
   `resolveNativeSeatLaunch` fresh read → `resolveNativeSeatDisplayMetadata`
   cached read) against the actual host volume. On hosts where the bounded
   reads complete, it asserts the full positive path; where they cannot, it
   asserts documented fail-closed refusal — never a guessed identity.
   File added to `REAL_IO_TEST_FILES` (test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs):
   it now performs real I/O and belongs in the serialized real-io lane.

4. **Staging-stop — assert both settled and unattempted reports**
   `test/fleet-staging-batch-stop-05sta2.test.ts`: `--json` assertion now
   checks the settled `/fake/a` report AND the `/fake/b`
   `{complete: false, source: 'unattempted'}` report; `--text` assertion now
   checks the `skipped (unattempted)` line. Production already emitted both —
   the old assertion was stale.

## Dropped / stale

- **No production changes for staging-stop**: the unattempted report emission
  already exists on current HEAD (`fleet-staging-inventory-batch.ts`); only the
  stale assertion needed updating.
- **Boot-identity fail-closed**: already covered by
  `test/resource-native-boot-identity.test.ts` ("does not launch commands on
  unsupported platform linux/win32/freebsd") — not re-added.
- **Linux `/proc` foreign-pid fallback**: already implemented in
  `verifiedProcessStartIdentity` and covered by `m416.local-store-lock-handoff`
  — not re-added.

## Environment limitation (not a regression)

`/bin/ps` is denied by this host's sandbox (`bash: /bin/ps: Operation not
permitted`). The own-pid custody fix makes own-lease verification work anyway;
the two `resource-quota-native-lifecycle` real-io tests now advance past the
lease stage but still cannot complete here because the durable launch proof
requires `/bin/ps` inside the spawned launcher child (by design — signed
kernel child identity). They are expected to pass on hosts permitting ps.
Similarly `resource-quota-launch-handoff` (15) and one
`resource-quota-shared-evidence` test require foreign/child kernel probes and
remain environment-blocked. `diskutil` also ran ~1.1–1.5s on this loaded host
(fixed 1s spawn bound), so the real-host volume test exercised the fail-closed
branch here.

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-MERGEBATCH-1

## What

`phm fleet merge-batch [--input <file>|-] [--repo <owner/name>] [--root <abs>] [--json]`
— a read-only merge-batch planner for the merge treadmill (~180 open bridge
PRs invalidating each other as main moves hourly).

- `src/core/fleet/merge-batch.ts` (new, 540 LOC): pure planner, no I/O.
  Parses three real snapshot shapes — a raw `gh pr list --json` array
  (`number,title,headRefName,isDraft,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,createdAt,updatedAt,files`),
  a merge-backlog read `{v:1, items}` and a `fleet.pr-hygiene.v1` report —
  carrying the envelope's own read state (`input.upstream`), then builds the
  file-overlap graph: connected components become batches.
  Disjoint (independent) batches merge in any order/concurrently; serial
  batches get an order that minimizes rebase events = members − max
  independent set (greedy min-degree MIS, ties keep wide diffs clean),
  clean wave FIFO first, rebase wave least-ready last. Per-batch
  `conflictRisk` (0..1, documented formula) + `reasons`, hot files (≥3
  fan-in), and a flattened `order`. Emits `fleet.merge-batch.v1`.
- `src/cli/fleet-merge-batch.ts` (new, 237 LOC): thin CLI. Input precedence
  `--input` → piped stdin → `<root>/fleet/open-prs.json`
  (ASHLR_RUNS_DIR/`--root`, default ~/.ashlr-runs). Bounded 32 MiB reads.
  No gh calls anywhere. Exit 0 plan, 1 no usable snapshot (`input.state`
  honest: missing/unreadable/too-large/malformed — or the envelope's own
  upstream read failed, `input.upstream`), 2 usage. Classifies
  `read` in the fleet verb catalog.
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts`: regenerated (gen-fleet-registry).
- `src/cli/completions.ts`: `merge-batch` added to the fleet verb list.
- `src/cli/fleet-usage.ts` (+4/−1): drive-by — declared the missing
  `const usage` the registry-help test requires; the pre-existing suite
  failure (`verb "usage" has non-empty help text`) now passes. Error text
  changed `usage:` → `Usage:`; exit codes unchanged.
- `test/fleet-pr-batching.test.ts` (new, 370 LOC, 31 tests): named to keep
  the basename free of Tier-1 test stems (`merge` is one; a `*-merge-*`
  name would need a generated `.github/CODEOWNERS` line this job may not
  add). Covers parser shapes, dedupe/unreadable, star/clique batching,
  clean-wave exclusion for conflicted/BEHIND/draft PRs, FIFO and
  readiness ordering, hot files, risk ordering, and the CLI input paths.
- `docs/FLEET-MERGE-BATCH.md` (new, 73 LOC), `docs/FLEET-VERBS.md` row,
  `docs/README.md` index link (absolute URL — source-only doc, same
  convention as other unpackaged guides).

## Design notes

- Min rebases = batch size − clean-wave size: every PR ordered after an
  overlapping neighbour rebases once against accumulated main, so an
  independent set merges clean and the rest rebase once each.
- A zero-file PR is an independent batch with `evidence: 'no-file-data'` —
  unmeasured overlap, never silently proven-disjoint. `conflicted`/
  `BEHIND`/draft PRs can never join the clean wave (`rebase:
  'already-required'`).
- Batches sort safest-first; disjoint batches may still merge concurrently —
  the flat `order` is the serial-safe sequence, not a claim one is needed.

title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-TOCTOU-RACE-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-TOCTOU-RACE-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `5344526f3`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-TOCTOU-RACE-1

Security follow-up to merged PR #4002 (RQ-SWE3-SEC-PATHS-1). Closes the
remaining intermediate-symlink TOCTOU in `readUnmetDeps`/`readDepPrompt`
(src/core/fleet/runs-parked-queue.ts) and hardens the two test gaps the job
named.

## What changed

### src/core/fleet/runs-parked-queue.ts (+54 / −6 net)

`readDepPrompt` previously proved containment with name-based checks that each
re-walked the mutable namespace: `open(resolved, O_NOFOLLOW)` → `realpath(resolved)`
→ `lstat(resolved)` dev/ino match. An attacker flipping an intermediate
symlink outside-for-open / inside-for-realpath / outside-for-lstat satisfied
every check while the descriptor read an outside file's DEPENDENCY GATE.

Containment is now proven against the held descriptor:

- `descriptorPath()` returns `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` on Linux/Android — realpath
  of an fd path is kernel truth about the pinned inode; a resolved answer that
  sits outside the root rejects outright.
- Portable POSIX bind: re-`open()` the **canonical** spelling
  (`realpath(resolved)` output carries no symlinks, so the flip cannot steer
  this second resolution) and require `dev`/`ino` equality with the opened fd.
  The flip can steer `open()` or `realpath()` but cannot make the canonical
  name resolve to the same outside inode — verified deterministically below.
- Post-read fence: `lstat(resolved)` identity must still match the fd and
  `realpath(resolved)` must be unchanged, so observed namespace churn
  discards the bytes (fail closed, matches the tree's documented
  changed-during-read doctrine).
- `O_NOFOLLOW`/`O_NONBLOCK` now follow the repo's `typeof === 'number'` guard
  idiom (stable-file-read.ts) instead of bare constants.

Documented residual (unchanged, acknowledged in-tree elsewhere): Node has no
portable openat(2)/F_GETPATH, so a same-user attacker renaming *real*
directories can still race probes — the before/after checks make those swaps
observable and fail closed.

### test/fleet-runs-parked-unmet-deps.test.ts (+79 / −5 net)

- Deterministic race regression test: `vi.mock('node:fs/promises')` retargets
  `runs/queue/link` to outside for `open()`/`lstat()` and inside for
  `realpath()` at exactly the syscalls the exploit needed — no timing. Verified
  it fails on the pre-fix code (emitted `RQ-LEAK`) and passes on the fix.
- Oversized-file test now has read-byte assertions: `RQ-IN` ends inside the
  64 KiB window, `RQ-TAIL` sits wholly past it — the former unbounded
  `readFile` would have surfaced `RQ-TAIL`.
- All existing tests untouched in intent; mock is inert unless `raceCtl.active`.

## Verification (all with temporary HOME, hermetic)

| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` (foreground, once) | PASS — file selection, `tsc --noEmit`, realio lane lint, verse sync-I/O lint, dedupe `8fa42ced97f9`. eslint skipped: `node_modules/eslint` absent in worktree (Merge Gate lints on CI) |

| `npx vitest run test/fleet-runs-parked-unmet-deps.test.ts` (+5 fleet files: parked-queue-oct31, parked-queue-repo-mix, parked-queue-next-up, fleet-status-api, fleet-live-queue-route-oct31) | PASS — 6 files, 29/29 tests |
| `npm run test:ci -- test/fleet-runs-parked-unmet-deps.test.ts` | PASS — 11/11 |

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-NPM-ETARGET-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `5344526f3`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-NPM-ETARGET-1

## Summary

npm C24 ETARGET follow-up. After the #3835 install-catalog gate
(`reconcileRegistry` waits for the abbreviated `install-v1` catalog to show the
version), the exact-version `npm install` in `publish-canonical-npm.yml` still
hit `ETARGET` — the reconciled HTTP read and npm's own packument resolution can
sit on different registry replicas, so catalog readiness alone is insufficient.

This change adds a bounded retry for the no-scripts install/read path:

- `scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs`
  - `installPublishedArgs(version)` — the same command the consumer
    verification runs (`npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
    --save-exact --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org @ashlr/phantom@<v>`)
    plus `--prefer-online`, so each retry revalidates the packument over the
    network instead of replaying a locally cached (stale) response.
  - `installPublishedPackage(record, directory, deps)` — runs that install in a
    scratch consumer dir (creates a minimal private `package.json` if the
    caller did not `npm init` one), retries **ETARGET only** up to
    `INSTALL_ETARGET_ATTEMPTS = 4` total attempts with 5s/10s/20s backoff
    (~35s worst-case added latency), then holds. Every other failure — and any
    output mixing ETARGET with EINTEGRITY/EPROVENANCE/E401/E403/ENEEDAUTH —
    throws immediately with a bounded output tail. Nothing is suppressed and
    nothing is republished.
  - Post-install proof: `node_modules/@ashlr/phantom/package.json` name+version
    must equal the admitted record, and `node_modules/.package-lock.json`'s
    resolved `integrity` must equal `record.integrity` — a substituted or
    downgraded tree holds (stronger than the workflow's version-only check).
  - New CLI verb: `canonical-npm-publisher.mjs install <admittedDir>
    <consumerDir>` — verifies the handoff hashes exactly like the sibling
    verbs, then performs the bounded-retry install.
- `test/canonical-npm-publisher.test.ts` — new `no-scripts consumer install`
  describe (14 tests): exact argv, manifest creation/preservation, ETARGET
  retry+backoff+logging, bounded exhaustion, no-retry on
  integrity/provenance/auth/mixed/other failures, and version/integrity
  post-install holds.

## Required paired wiring (Security-owned `.github/` — NOT done here)

`.github/**` is `@masonwyatt23`-owned and this job's hard rules forbid editing
it, so the two bare `npm install` call sites need a paired pin that swaps them
for the new verb:

- `publish` job, step `Verify publisher provenance without executing candidate
  code` — replace the `npm init --yes` + `npm install --ignore-scripts ...
  "@ashlr/phantom@$VERSION"` + `test "$(node -p ...)" = "$VERSION"` lines with:

  ```bash
  mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer"
  node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs" install \
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-npm-admitted" "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer"
  ```

  (keep the following `cd`, `npm audit signatures`, and `provenance` lines).

- `consumer` job, step `Verify isolated public installed CLI` — replace the
  `env -i ... npm install --ignore-scripts ... "@ashlr/phantom@$VERSION"` line
  with:

  ```bash
  env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-home" \
    NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG="$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-npmrc" \
    node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs" install \
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-npm-admitted" "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer"
  ```

  (keep the `ashlr --version` assertion; note it must then run from
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer`, or point at
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer/node_modules/@ashlr/phantom/bin/ashlr`).

Until that pin lands the workflow behavior is unchanged; the verb is exercised
by the new tests and a stubbed-npm e2e below.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/canonical-npm-publisher.test.ts` —
  **71/71 passed** (14 new).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS (file selection,
  tsc --noEmit, realio lane lint, verse sync-I/O lint, dedupe). eslint SKIP:
  `node_modules/eslint/lib/cli.js` absent in this worktree; Merge Gate lints on
  CI. WARN: two pre-existing unrelated unchanged-file lane-lint notes.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run check:docs` — errors: `[]`.
- `node --check scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs` — syntax OK.
- Manual e2e with a stubbed `npm` on PATH: 2×ETARGET (real 5s/10s backoff) then
  success — `exit=0`, installed tree + auto manifest verified; permanent
  ETARGET exhausted at 4 attempts and threw with the npm output tail.
- No git/gh writes; `.github/` untouched; hermetic tests only (tmpdir +
  injected exec/sleep; no real HOME, registry, or credentials).

## Net LOC

`+194 / -2` — `scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs` +82,
`test/canonical-npm-publisher.test.ts` +112/−2. Two files changed.

## Notes for the closer

- The same-runner build+smoke path (RQ-CI-SAME-RUNNER-SMOKE-NOV7) is untouched;

# RQ-RECUTSCOPEQ8

Recuts now validate the observed PR's original merge base and commit range before creating a worktree. Refuse rewritten base history, changed or ambiguous merge bases, merge commits, empty history, and more than 100 original commits. Pin worktree creation to the validated fetched base SHA. Measure original and staged diffs independently: at most 100 files and 2,000 added/deleted lines, with binary/unmeasured changes refused. The final staged paths must belong to the original PR. Existing conflict, protected-path, verification and push controls remain enforced.

Five new integration cases exercise oversized conflict resolution, oversized source changes, merged unrelated work, a base that absorbs the head after observation, and rewritten unrelated base history. Existing tests cover successful divergent histories and confined conflict resolution, plus rejection of edits outside conflicts.

Validation commands and results:

- `npm install -g @ashlr/phantom`: failed EPERM at the configured global prefix; existing installed `phm` used for read-only setup.
- `phm docs --agent --json`, `phm mcp list --json`, `phm wire status --json`: completed. Wire status reports unavailable/unwired clients; no config changes made. No companion MCP tools called.
- `npm run install:worktree`: passed; repaired incomplete installed ESLint files.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/autopilot.test.ts`: final run passed, 41 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped (1 file). Earlier runs passed 38 and 40 tests during development.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/autopilot.test.ts -t 'fetched base absorbed'`: passed, 1 selected test; 40 filtered tests.
- `npm run typecheck`: passed, backend and web.
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs`: final source tree passed changed-file ESLint, tsgo, realio lane and verse sync-I/O checks. Existing unrelated realio warnings in two unchanged tests. Earlier run reported missing ESLint before dependency repair.
- `npm run check:docs`: passed, 0 errors.
- `npm run lint`: initially failed due to incomplete ESLint installation; repaired rerun completed ESLint (0 errors, 262 existing warnings), then failed the pre-existing real-I/O lane membership check for unchanged `test/ecosystem-changelog-generator.test.ts` and `test/verse-standby-python-contract-02somp1.test.ts`. The final verse check was covered by verify-changed. No unrelated gate or test was changed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Net source/test LOC: +96 (97 additions, 1 deletion). Including these 22 bridge-note lines: net +118 LOC.

Conservative limits: merged PR histories and binary changes require manual handling rather than automatic recut. No semantic intent inference is attempted for unrelated changes already included as ordinary original PR commits. No commit, push, tag, publish, workflow or credential changes made.
</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-SWE3-APP-SPIN-1 handoff

Both the desktop computer relay and browser agent relay immediately repeat successful command polls. Their server endpoints normally long-poll, but an immediately responding endpoint can drive an unbounded request loop. Each loop now waits 250 ms after a successful poll; stopping or hiding it aborts the wait. Regression tests exercise rapid empty responses and shutdown. This is a defensive fix; the reported 166% CPU incident was not reproduced or attributed to these loops. A profile of the affected process is still needed to establish its cause. `ps` was denied by the host, and no live application profile was obtained.

title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-APIBENCH-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-APIBENCH-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `1048a4e06`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs test/perf-budget.test.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-APIBENCH-1

## Summary

CLI/MCP startup benchmark + targeted shaving. Measured `phm --help`,
`phm status`, `phm doctor`, and MCP `tools/list` latency on this machine,
found the dominant startup costs, and cut them without touching any
bounded-timeout, fail-closed, or secret-handling behavior.

### Startup-cost offenders found (this machine, instrumented)

1. **V8 compile of the dist module graph** — ~250 ms of a `phm --version`
   profile was pure compile; every command paid it (~900 ms medians).
2. **Eager handler dependency graph in `src/core/mcp-native.ts`** — the MCP
   gateway loaded ~899 modules before answering `initialize`; ~337 of them
   came from static imports only needed inside handlers (dashboard.js,
   seams/index.js, orient.js, quality/health.js, …). `tools/list` only needs
   schemas + safety gates.
3. **Eager `yaml` in `src/core/mcp-gateway-policy.ts`** — pulled ~50 modules
   even with no policy file configured (zod is already loaded by the MCP SDK).
4. **Serial probe sections in `phm status`** — the tools registry ran serial
   `which` + `--version` probes per tool (~0.5 s each on this box), and
   MCP discovery used the synchronous `~/.claude.json` parser. With one
   tracked repo, `phm status` was ~4.5 s.
5. **Serial tail in `phm doctor`** — `checkPlugins` and `checkLocalInference`
   awaited after the parallel wave instead of inside it; `locusAvailable()`
   spawned `which locus` twice.

### Changes

- `bin/ashlr`: call `module.enableCompileCache()` before importing the CLI —
  content-addressed V8 cache for the dist graph; failure can never break
  startup (try/catch + optional call).
- `src/cli/index.ts` (`cmdStatus`): switch to `getToolsRegistry({parallel:true})`
  and `discoverMcpServersAsync()`; launch all best-effort probes and lazy
  module imports up front so spawned children and module compilation overlap
  the serial sections. Print order unchanged; every probe failure resolves
  to `null` exactly as before.
- `src/cli/status.ts` (`gatherStatus`): all best-effort sections now run via
  `Promise.all` instead of serial `await`s (same object shape, same order).
  `StatusLoaders` invoker types widened to allow promise-returning probes
  (injected sync loaders still satisfy it).
- `src/core/doctor.ts`: moved `checkPlugins`/`checkLocalInference` into the
  existing `Promise.all` wave (report order unchanged; neither can reject);
  one `locusAvailable()` result now serves `checkLocus` + `checkLocusFirm`
  via a new optional `available` param (signatures stay compatible);
  `prewarmDoctor` warms the plugin modules too.
- `src/core/mcp-native.ts`: 17 handler-only imports converted to `await
  import()` inside their handlers. Static imports retained only where the
  tool DEFINITIONS or `callNativeTool`'s structural gates need them
  synchronously (schemas, `killSwitchOn`, `audit`, scrub/textResult output
  hygiene, drop-job/fleet-app enums) plus `listProposals`/`readDecisions`
  behind the synchronous `deriveRoutingData` contract. Gateway import graph:
  899 → 213 modules.
- `src/core/mcp-gateway-policy.ts`: `yaml` now loaded via `createRequire`
  inside `parseGatewayPolicy` — only reached when `ASHLR_MCP_POLICY` names a
  file. Still fail-closed: any load/parse error throws and refuses startup.
- `perf/budgets.json` + `scripts/perf-budget.mjs`: added `phm-help` and
  `phm-mcp-tools-list` targets (the latter times
  `scripts/perf-mcp-tools-list.mjs`, a new stdio handshake harness:
  initialize → notifications/initialized → tools/list).
- Tests: new `test/perf-mcp-tools-list.test.ts` (handshake on scratch HOME;
  non-zero exit without dist), new `test/bin-ashlr-entry.test.ts`
  (compile-cache resilience incl. unusable cache path), updated
  `test/perf-budget.test.ts` target list, registered both new files in
  `test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs` (real-io lane).

### Measured on this machine (macOS arm64, node runner, fresh HOME)

| command              | before (median)         | after (median) | note |
|----------------------|-------------------------|----------------|------|
| `phm --version`      | ~840–880 ms             | **104 ms**     |      |
| `phm --help`         | ~1200–1700 ms           | **114 ms**     |      |
| `phm status` (0 repo)| ~900–2000 ms            | **114 ms**     |      |
| `phm status` (1 repo)| ~4500 ms                | **~850 ms**    | parallel probes |
| `phm doctor`         | ~7700 ms                | **396 ms**     |      |
| MCP `tools/list`     | ~4400–5300 ms           | **345 ms**     | initialize+list; list itself ~3 ms |

Post-change single-shot with fresh compile cache: version 133 ms, help
109 ms, status 136 ms, doctor 676 ms, tools/list 507 ms. This machine has
abnormally slow, noisy I/O (bare `node -e ""` ≈ 400–600 ms); expect
different absolute numbers elsewhere — the direction is what matters.

Budgets for the two new targets are seeded at CI-runner-class estimates
(help 600 ms, mcp-tools-list 3000 ms), matching the file's existing
convention; re-baseline on the real runner with `--update-baseline`.

## Files changed

- `bin/ashlr` (+8)
- `src/cli/index.ts` — cmdStatus probe launch + parallel loaders
- `src/cli/status.ts` — parallel gatherStatus + StatusLoaders types
- `src/core/doctor.ts` — wave membership, locus dedup, prewarm
- `src/core/mcp-native.ts` — lazy handler imports
- `src/core/mcp-gateway-policy.ts` — lazy yaml via createRequire
- `perf/budgets.json` — 2 new targets
- `scripts/perf-budget.mjs` — doc comment
- `scripts/perf-mcp-tools-list.mjs` — NEW handshake harness
- `test/perf-budget.test.ts` — expected target ids/files
- `test/perf-mcp-tools-list.test.ts` — NEW
- `test/bin-ashlr-entry.test.ts` — NEW
- `test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs` — lane entries for new tests

Net LOC: **+325** (tracked diff +252/−169, plus 242 lines in 3 new files).

## Commands run

- `npx tsc -b` — clean
- `npm run typecheck:fast` (tsgo, backend + web) — PASS
- `npx eslint <changed files>` — PASS (node_modules was partially installed;
  `node scripts/worktree-install.mjs` healed eslint first)
- `npm run check:docs` — PASS (0 errors)
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS (all gates; second run recorded
  tree dedupe)
- `npm run test:ci -- <suites>` / `npx vitest run <file>` with fresh HOME
- `node scripts/perf-budget.mjs --home $(mktemp -d) --runner node --runs 5 [--json]`
- `node scripts/perf-mcp-tools-list.mjs` on scratch HOMEs
- Exploration subagent audited the refactor (no blocking findings)

## Test results

Pass: 11-file m31/mcp-native/mcp-gateway batch **131/131**; doctor batch
(m2.doctor 57, locus-launcher 5, exit-code 4, local-inference 16,
mcp-gateway-policy 10, lazy-start, routing-data, dedupe, ecosystem,
h7.probes, phantom-preflight) all green; new tests 17/17 (perf-budget,
perf-mcp-tools-list, bin-ashlr-entry). cli-help/no-side-effects suites green.

**Pre-existing failures (verified identical on unmodified base, not this
diff):**

- `test/cli-status-json.test.ts` — 1 test: `status --json` live-key
  assertion predates this change (output gained `lanes`/`repos`/`summary`).
- `test/m20.doctor-fix.test.ts` — 11 tests fail only in large multi-file
  runs: the file's `spawn` mock emits an unlistened `'error'` event (52
  unhandled errors even solo); fails identically on base with the same file
  set. Solo: 23/23 pass.

## Safety notes

- Gateway policy remains fail-closed (unreadable/invalid policy refuses
  startup; yaml failure throws inside the same error message).
- All previously bounded probes keep their timeouts; loopback-only local
  inference probe unchanged (3 s cap, 256 KiB cap, no auth headers).
- Structural MCP gates (kill switch, arg validation, audit, output scrub +
  32 KB cap) are untouched and still synchronous in `callNativeTool`.
- No `.github/` edits, no secrets printed, no workflow/permission changes.
- All changes are uncommitted; nothing pushed or published.
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-TESTSPEED-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-TESTSPEED-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `1048a4e06`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/resource-engineering-preparation-acceptance.test.ts test/resource-engineering-setup-acceptance.test.ts test/resource-pool-evolution-engineering.test.ts test/setup/home.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-SWE3-TESTSPEED-1 — Test-suite speed audit & safe wins

## Summary

Audited the Vitest suite (3,384 test files across `unit`, `real-io`, and
`serial-cpu` projects) and CI lanes for wall-time sinks, then implemented one
safe, reviewable optimization: **Node compile cache for spawned test children**.

Six heavyweight acceptance/integration files spawn `node --import tsx` children
per launch and had explicitly set `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE: '1'`, forcing
every child to recompile the same modules. The disables are removed so those
children inherit a **worker-private** `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` installed by
`test/setup/home.ts` (a tmpdir sibling of the isolated worker HOME — *not*
inside it, because tests snapshot `homedir()` to prove fixtures untouched). The
cache is created once per worker process, shared by every inheriting child, and
removed on worker exit under the same custody checks as the worker home.

`test/universe-backlog-marker-evaluator.test.ts` keeps an explicit,
fixture-private cache (`<base>/node-compile-cache`) because its child env is
fully pinned (no `process.env` spread) and per-test isolated.

Measured on this host (18-core arm64, Node v26.9.0, load avg ~50-70 during the
run — see caveats):

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| tsx child boot+import (`src/cli/universe-controller.ts`), 8 spawns | 3,799 ms/child | 2,550 ms/child (**−33%**, ≈1.25 s saved per child) |

Earlier unloaded measurement of the same mechanism showed ~0.4-0.5 s/child
savings; the gain grows under contention. For the `real-io` lane (675 files,
~92 files spawning tsx children), each removed disable converts every child
launch in the file from cold-compile to warm-cache.

## Top-10 time sinks (from profiling + static analysis)

Profiling inputs: `vitest --reporter=json` sample run
(`/tmp/phm-profile/sample.json`), `isolatedSeconds` measured-duration table,
`ASHLR_ACCEPTANCE_PHASE_TIMING`/`ASHLR_ENGINEERING_SETUP_PHASE_TIMING`
instrumented run of `resource-engineering-setup-acceptance`, static counts
(`rg`), and direct child-process benchmarks. Host was heavily contended
(load 50-70 on 18 cores) — absolute numbers inflated, ordering reliable.

1. **Deadline-bound real campaign waits.** `resource-engineering-setup-acceptance`
   spends 300,765 ms in `delivery.wait` (single call, deadline-bound E2E), plus
   `console.bootstrap` 19.6 s and `cli.prepare-or-replay` 34.6 s. **Intentional**
   E2E behavior — not safely removable.
2. **tsx child-process boot.** ~92 test files spawn `node --import tsx`
   children; measured 3.8 s/child under load (2.9 s unloaded). tsx 4.x has no
   disk cache. **Addressed**: worker-private `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` cuts ~33%.
3. **Long-interval polling loops.** `console.read` cost 59.3 s across 494 polls
   plus repeated `until()`/ready-wait loops (25-500 ms intervals) across
   acceptance files. Convergence speed is bounded by poll interval × number of
   waits.
4. **m342.dispatch-production-ledger churn cases.** 1,525 s for the file under
   load; single cases up to 205 s of in-process ledger churn (real algorithmic
   work, serial-cpu lane by design).
5. **m201.daemon-loop.** 753 s under load — 243 tests of real daemon event
   loops.
6. **Per-invocation Vitest floor.** A trivial 1-file run shows ~3 s of tests
   inside a ~16 s wall clock (~12 s startup) on the contended host — forked
   workers, config load, and transform dominate small invocations.
7. **Collection cost.** `vitest list`/collection across 3,384 files exceeded
   5 min before termination — collection alone is a CI-inventory bottleneck.
8. **Repeated git-repo fixtures.** 222 files run `git init`+add+commit per
   test/file — each is a chain of real subprocess spawns (~80 ms+ per git call
   measured in fixture timing).
9. **Fixture sprawl.** 1,963 files create per-test `mkdtemp` trees; heavy files
   re-mkdtemp and re-git-init per test rather than per suite.
10. **Sequential serialization of the heavy tail.** `serial-cpu` lane is
    `maxWorkers: 1` with `fileParallelism: false`, and the real-io lane is 2
    workers — the heaviest measured files run effectively serial (intentional
    isolation for git index locks/subprocess contention; documented policy in
    `src/core/run/tool-path.ts`, not a safe knob to turn on shared hosts).

Rejected approaches, with evidence:

- **esbuild-bundling CLI/controller modules for children** (pattern from
  `test/helpers/policy-child-bundle.ts`): bundles `import.meta.url`-dependent
  code; the codebase intentionally branches on `import.meta.url.endsWith('.ts')`
  (`automerge-canary-observer.ts` chooses tsx loader vs plain node for nested
  children) and resolves `../../../scripts/evaluators/*` and `../../package.json`
  by depth. Verified failure: bundled `universe-controller` child produced
  `campaign-failed` where the source child passes.
- **Native `--experimental-strip-types`**: can't resolve `.js`→`.ts` specifier
  rewriting (NodeNext). Confirmed: `node --experimental-strip-types
  src/cli/index.ts --version` fails to resolve `src/core/config.js`.
- **Raising worker counts**: `TEST_MAX_WORKERS = 4` and lane caps are a
  deliberate memory/oversubscription policy; this host ran at load 50-70 —
  more parallelism would regress.

## Files changed

- `test/setup/home.ts` (+36): once-per-worker `enableCompileCache` into a
  worker-private tmpdir sibling (`ashlr-vitest-ncc-*`), `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE`
  re-asserted per test module, same-parity exit cleanup as the worker home.
  `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE` still wins anywhere it is explicitly set.
- `test/resource-console-engineering-inspect.test.ts` (−1/+1)
- `test/resource-engineering-preparation-acceptance.test.ts` (−1/+1)
- `test/resource-engineering-setup-acceptance.test.ts` (−1/+1)
- `test/resource-pool-evolution-engineering.test.ts` (−1/+1)
- `test/universe-hub-marker-campaign.test.ts` (−1/+1)
- `test/universe-backlog-marker-evaluator.test.ts` (−1/+1): pinned-env child now
  uses fixture-private `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` instead of disabling.

Net LOC: **+42 −6 = +36** across 7 files. No test cases, assertions, or test
selection changed — zero coverage loss.

## Commands run

```sh
# profile
node scripts/slowest-tests.mjs /tmp/phm-profile/sample.json
ASHLR_ACCEPTANCE_PHASE_TIMING=1 ASHLR_ENGINEERING_SETUP_PHASE_TIMING=1 \
  npx vitest run test/resource-engineering-setup-acceptance.test.ts
node /tmp/child-boot-bench.mjs   # 8× spawnSync tsx children, cache on/off

# verification
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/setup/home.test.ts \
  test/universe-backlog-marker-evaluator.test.ts \
  test/resource-console-engineering-inspect.test.ts --reporter=dot
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/resource-engineering-preparation-acceptance.test.ts
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/resource-engineering-setup-acceptance.test.ts
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/resource-pool-evolution-engineering.test.ts \
  test/universe-hub-marker-campaign.test.ts
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/setup/*.test.ts
npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
npx eslint <7 changed files>
git stash && <same failing files on clean tree> && git stash pop
```

## Pass/fail counts

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test/setup/*.test.ts` (home, git-env, home-isolation-guard) | 21/21 pass |
| backlog-marker-evaluator + console-engineering-inspect + home | 50/50 pass |
| `resource-engineering-setup-acceptance` | 2 fail — "deadline-exhausted" on the deadline-bound real campaign (same signature observed pre-edit in the instrumented run: `delivery.wait` = 300.8 s timeout). Load-induced, not this change. |
| `resource-engineering-preparation-acceptance` | 1 fail — "Prepared fixture did not complete" (45 s deadline). **Reproduces identically on clean tree** — load-induced environmental flake, not this change. |
| `resource-pool-evolution-engineering`, `universe-hub-marker-campaign` | 3 fails — "Cannot establish campaign process ownership" (`/bin/ps` 1 s probe budget exceeded under load 50-70). **Reproduces identically on clean tree** (verified via `git stash` + rerun). |
| `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` | **all PASS** (file selection, eslint changed files, tsgo --noEmit, realio-lane lint, verse sync-io lint, verify dedupe). |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` (7 files) | clean |

Supplementary: `shard-1-of-4.json` (parallel profile) confirms the heavy tail
is the real-io acceptance suites — `resource-engineering-setup-acceptance`
739.8 s, `resource-engineering-supervisor-acceptance` 259.4 s,
`memory-benchmark` 253.3 s, `m360.generated-repair-lifecycle` 242.6 s —
plus serial-cpu benchmark files, all dominated by real subprocess/campaign
work, not fixable fixture overhead.

## Caveats

- Host load was 50-70 throughout; absolute wall times are inflated and some
  real-io acceptance tests flake on their fixed `/bin/ps` 1-second probe
  budget (`verifiedProcessStartRef`). Those flakes exist on HEAD.
- The win is per-child (~1.2 s under load, ~0.5 s unloaded) × number of
  `node --import tsx` children per file; biggest in multi-launch files
  (e.g. `universe-controller-drain-integration` spawns ~12+).
- Changes left uncommitted as required. Full 4-shard profile was still running
  under load at handoff; `sample.json` and `shard-1-of-4.json` are the
  harvested evidence.
- Environment note: the worktree's `node_modules/eslint` shipped without
  `lib/` (broken install, unrelated to this change); repaired via
  `npm install eslint@<pinned version> --no-save` — untracked, does not
  appear in `git status`.
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-SEC-PATHS-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-SEC-PATHS-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `ac173499c`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-SEC-PATHS-1

## Summary

Teammate-reported security findings in the parked-queue reader were confirmed
and fixed in `readUnmetDeps` / new `readDepPrompt` helper in
`src/core/fleet/runs-parked-queue.ts`. The reader is reached by
`fleetStatusApi` (`src/core/fleet/status-api.ts`) and
`/api/verse/fleet/live/queue` (`src/core/verse/fleet-live-api.ts`), and the
untrusted `promptPath` comes straight from `ready.tsv` cells.

Confirmed vulnerabilities (all three reproduced):

1. **Absolute-path `..` escape**: absolute `promptPath` values were used
   unnormalized, so `/runs/../outside/x` passed the `startsWith(runsDir + '/')`
   string check while escaping the runs dir.
2. **In-root symlinks followed out**: `readFile` followed symlinks, so a
   symlink (final component or intermediate dir) inside the runs dir pointing
   outside it was read.
3. **Size cap applied after read**: `readFile` loaded the entire file, then
   `text.slice(0, MAX_PROMPT)` — unbounded memory use on a hostile prompt file.

Fix — `readDepPrompt` mirrors the descriptor-custody pattern in
`src/core/web/static.ts`:

- `resolve()` normalizes the path (absolute, or queue-relative for relative
  values); lexical containment vs `resolve(root)` rejects `..` escapes before
  the filesystem is touched.
- `open(O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK)` refuses a symlinked final
  component outright; `fstat` requires a regular file.
- `realpath(resolved)` must stay inside `realpath(root)` — symlinked
  intermediate components resolving outside are rejected, verified while the
  descriptor is held (bytes are never read through a separately checked
  pathname). `realpath(root)` is computed once per call; failure closes the
  reader (`unmetDeps` falls back to `[]`).
- `lstat` dev/ino must match the open descriptor (rename-swap guard).
- The read is bounded by `min(fstat.size, MAX_PROMPT)` bytes via positional
  reads on the descriptor — the 64 KiB cap is enforced before/during the read.
- Early `break` once 50 `unmetDeps` rows are collected (identical output to
  the old collect-then-`slice(0, 50)`, bounded fs work).

Behavior notes: DEP prompts that are symlinked final components are now
refused even when they resolve inside the runs dir (stricter than the literal
"don't follow out" requirement, matching `web/static.ts` custody semantics).
Regular-file prompts, missing files, directories and oversized files behave
as before (oversized prompts still parse their first 64 KiB).

## Files changed

- `src/core/fleet/runs-parked-queue.ts` (+45 / -14): hardened prompt read in
  `readUnmetDeps`; added private `readDepPrompt`; dropped unused `readFile`
  import; added `isAbsolute`, `resolve`, `sep`, `realpath` imports.

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-PRHYGIENE-1

## Summary

New read-only fleet verb `ashlr fleet pr-hygiene` that audits one repo's open
PRs and emits a `fleet.pr-hygiene.v1` machine-readable triage report for the
merge cockpit. Each PR is flagged `superseded` (same merged-job prompt
evidence as `fleet superseded`), `conflicted` (`mergeable: CONFLICTING` or
`mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`), `stale` (idle ≥ `--stale-days`, default 7),
`overlap` (shares files with other open PRs — tomorrow's conflict), `behind`
or `draft`, then triaged into one advisory lane: `close-candidate` >
`refix` > `review` > `ok`. Precedence is deliberate: a superseded PR is a
close candidate even when it also conflicts.

Evidence honesty per repo convention: a failed open-PR read still emits the
versioned shape with `reads.open: 'failed'`, empty items and an `error` token
(exit 1 — never a fake-clean backlog); a failed merged read or missing
prompts dir degrades only the superseded leg (`reads` records it); rows gh
could not describe are counted in `counts.unreadable`; unparseable
timestamps leave `ageDays`/`idleDays` null and are never flagged stale.

The verb catalogs as `read` under `fleet verbs` effect inference. Logic lives

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE2-DESKTOPCTL-1

## Summary

Desktop-app control, feature-flagged: `phm desktopctl` exposes Claude
Desktop, Codex Desktop, Devin Desktop and a running browser as
interchangeable desktop resources, driven entirely through the existing
`computer_*` MCP tool surface (injected `ToolCall` — nothing touches the
desktop natively).

- New `computer_permissions` MCP tool (first in the computer registry,
  read-only): relays the native `permissions` op — a TCC *preflight*
  (`CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess`, `AXIsProcessTrusted`,
  `CGPreflightPostEventAccess`) that reports Screen Recording /
  Accessibility / input-event grants and what each unlocks. It never shows
  a prompt and cannot grant; a `desktop-permissions:` machine line carries
  the state for programmatic readers. Lenient parser: unrecognized answers
  are `unknown`, never `granted`.
- `RunningApp.heldTier` + `parseRunningApps` now surface the per-chat grant
  tier `computer_list_apps` already reports ("this chat holds …").
- New `createBrowserDesktopAdapter` + `runningBrowserApp`: the browser as a
  read-only interchangeable resource (`start` always refuses; web actions
  stay in the Phantom Browser pane). `status`/`collect` read the
  accessibility tree only; collected text is scrubbed, capped and flagged
  `untrusted: true`.
- New `src/core/verse/desktopctl.ts`: strict flag parse
  (`~/.ashlr/desktopctl.json`, `{"enabled": true}`, optional
  `bundleIds` overrides for beta channels; missing file = off, malformed
  file = fail closed with the error reported), the `computer_permissions`
  probe, and `probeDesktopCapabilities` — per-resource
  `can {status,read,run}` plus machine `reasons` codes
  (`not-connected`, `flag-off`, `not-running`, `no-bundle-id`,
  `never-available`, `permission:accessibility`, `permission:post-events`,
  `not-granted`, `tier:insufficient`, `ceiling:insufficient`,
  `read-only-resource`, `unknown`). Missing Accessibility blocks
  everything; missing post-events blocks `run` only; a held `read`/`click`
  tier reads but cannot drive (driving presses controls and types, so it
  needs `full`); browsers never run.
- New `src/cli/desktopctl.ts` + dispatch/completions/help wiring:
  `capabilities`/`doctor` (read-only doctor — always runs, flag or not),
  `status <resource>`, `run <claude|codex|devin> --task <text>
  [--timeout s] [--poll s]`. Every verb writes start+result entries to the
  feed; if the start entry cannot be recorded the action is refused.
  Policy blocks → `refused`, environment blocks → `failed`; exit 0/1/2.

title: bridge: RQ-SWE-DESKPARITY-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE-DESKPARITY-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `6778b16f0`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/verse-workbench-contracts-310.test.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE-DESKPARITY-1

## Gap chosen

**The Files pane was a registry stub.** `docs/VERSE.md` said it plainly: "a
simple list of folders and touched files, not a file browser yet." Every
comparable agent desktop (Devin, Claude Code, Codex, Grok) ships a real file
explorer with preview. Phantom had everything else in the parity list —
live session status, diffs/PR review, run/stop, approvals, notifications,
queue, settings, usage/budget — but no way to look at the project tree.

This change makes the Files pane a real, read-only file browser:

- `POST /api/verse/files/browse {sessionId, root?, path?}` — one directory
  listing (≤256 entries), lazy per-directory.
- `POST /api/verse/files/read {sessionId, root?, path}` — a bounded UTF-8
  text preview (≤64 KiB, `truncated` flag when larger).

Both are POSTs inside the existing `session-controls` family, so they inherit
the workbench dispatch gate and the mutation token — browsing is a
*privileged read*: the pane shows an unlock row until the token is held, and
no file content ever reaches a model ("Add to message" quotes only the
`@path`, same as the touched-files rows).

## Alternatives considered

- **Per-chat usage/budget strip** — already covered: the usage surfaces and
  budget API exist; marginal gain.
- **Transcript search** — Sources/Reasoning panes and session search already
  cover retrieval; lower leverage than a missing whole surface.
- **Terminal/browser/diff polish** — all already at parity or beyond.
- **Full file *editor*** — editing, search-in-file, image previews are
  explicitly out of scope (documented in `docs/VERSE.md` known limits);
  read+preview is the coherent PR-sized slice.

## Implementation summary

Backend (`src/core/verse/`):

- `session-files.ts` (new, ~320 lines): async browse/read over the chat's
  own `verseSessionRoots`, each root re-validated per request by
  `checkWorkspaceRootPathAsync`. Containment is proven by realpath
  (`physicalPathAsync` + `isUnderPath`); a requested `root` must physical-
  match one of the chat's roots. Names are policy-filtered (no dotfiles but
  a small safe set, no credential/key/build-output names, strict UTF-8,
  no control chars). Listings are capped at 256 dirents (over-cap is a
  `LIMIT` 413, not silent truncation), directories-first sorted, entry stats
  fanned out at concurrency 8, and vanished/unreadable entries are skipped.
  Reads use `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, require a regular file owned by
  this uid, read at most 64 KiB, re-lstat the path against the opened
  dev/ino, re-prove containment, and reject non-UTF-8/control-byte content.
  Directory inode is re-verified after enumeration (lstat→opendir swap).
- `session-controls-api.ts`: `handleFilesReadRoute` validates bodies
  strictly (unknown keys → 400), maps `SessionFilesError` to
  `VERSE_INVALID`/400, `VERSE_FILE_NOT_FOUND`/404, `VERSE_FILE_LIMIT`/413,
  `VERSE_FILE_UNAVAILABLE`/503. `handleFiles` keeps GET = fuzzy finder and
  accepts only the exact POST browse/read paths.
- `workbench-types.ts`: route constants + request/response contracts.
  No digest field — a bare sha256 is secret-shaped to `sanitizePublicJson`
  and nothing consumes it; `sizeBytes`/`byteLength`/`truncated`/`path`
  already identify the snapshot.

Frontend (`src/web-ui/routes/verse/panes/builtin/`):

- `FileBrowser.tsx` (new): root picker chips (only with >1 root), lazy tree
  (expand fetches once; collapse/re-expand retries failures), per-directory
  loading/error rows, bounded preview card with size/truncation meta,
  "Add to message" (`@displayPath`), aborts stale fetches, resets on
  session/hold/root change, fetches nothing while hidden or unlocked.
- `file-browser-model.ts` + `file-browser-queries.ts` (new): pure
  flatten/state projection and the two `apiPost` calls.
- `FilesPane.tsx`: renders `<FileBrowser>` above the existing
  folders/touched-files sections (all prior behavior preserved).
- `stub-panes.module.css`: picker/tree/preview styles.

Docs: `docs/VERSE-CONTRACT-V1.md` route table, `docs/VERSE.md` pane table +
known-limits, `src/web-ui/routes/verse/panes/README.md` registry row.

## Commands run

All test runs used `HOME=$(mktemp -d)`.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | PASS (exit 0; backend tsc + web tsc) |
| `npm run typecheck:fast` (tsgo, re-run after final edit) | PASS (exit 0) |
| `npm run lint` | PASS — 0 errors, 261 pre-existing warnings in unrelated files |
| `npm run lint:verse-sync-io` | PASS — no sync fs/child-process in console route files |
| targeted `npx eslint` on all touched/new files | PASS — clean |
| `npm run check:docs` | PASS — 0 errors (252 local / 322 source / 118 external links) |
| `npm run test:ci -- test/verse-session-files.test.ts` | PASS — 15/15 |
| `npm run test:ci -- test/verse-session-controls-api-310.test.ts` | PASS — 12/12 |
| `npm run test:ci -- test/verse-workbench-contracts-310.test.ts` | 47/48 — see note |
| `npm run test:web -- src/web-ui/routes/verse/panes/builtin/` | PASS — 12/12 (3 files) |
| `git diff --check` | clean |

### Known environmental failure (pre-existing, not caused by this change)

`test/verse-workbench-contracts-310.test.ts` › "resolves a landed module to
its named handler" timed out at ~5006 ms vs the unit lane's 5000 ms default
on three runs. Verified by `git stash -u` A/B: the **same test fails
identically on the base tree** (5006 ms, 47/48 pass) — the box was at load
average ~104 on 18 cores, and this test sequentially dynamic-imports every
workbench module through the vitest transform pipeline. The new contract
assertions this change added to that file (route constants, segment
boundary) all pass. No test was weakened or skipped.

## Pass/fail counts

- Backend suites touched: **74/75 tests pass**
  (`verse-session-files` 15/15, `verse-session-controls-api-310` 12/12,
  `verse-workbench-contracts-310` 47/48 — the one failure is the
  environmental timeout above, reproduced identically on the base tree).
- Web suites touched: **12/12 pass** (3 files).
- Static checks: typecheck, typecheck:fast, lint, check:docs, sync-io
  guard, targeted eslint, `git diff --check` — all clean.

## Net LOC

**+1,448** (excluding this file):

- Production: ~+950 (session-files 319, FileBrowser 285, model 77,
  queries 49, session-controls-api +80/−2, workbench-types +53,
  FilesPane +10/−6, CSS +85)
- Tests: ~+495 (session-files.test 249, FileBrowser.test 121,
  model.test 68, api test +52/−1, contracts test +5)
- Docs: ~+13

## Left uncommitted

Per task rules: no commit, push, tag, or publish. All changes are in the
worktree on `codex-bridge/RQ-SWE-DESKPARITY-1`, ready for review.
</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-PLAN-BUS-THREADS-B

## Summary

Shared local task board for cooperating agents and machines, with durable bus
threads and task ownership backed by real fenced fleet queue claims.

- `src/core/fleet/shared-store.ts`: new `handoffClaim(ref, machineId)` transfers
  a live `claimed` lease under the existing queue lock. It allocates a fresh
  epoch and owner token, rewrites the owner key, and fences the previous
  capability. It refuses expired, executing, exact-match-failing, same-owner,
  invalid and oversized recipients; returns `null` on lock contention or an
  unreadable queue rather than mutating state.
- `src/core/fleet/bus-delivery.ts` (new): durable delivery record with v1
  envelope routing metadata, thread ID, sender, recipient, ISO timestamp and
  `content.trust: 'untrusted'`. `presentBusBoardText` rewraps content under a
  fresh unpredictable delimiter on every read; `busBoardHop` projects
  metadata-only hops (id, thread, sender, recipient, timestamp).
- `src/core/fleet/bus-board.ts` (new): `BusBoard` persists threads, tasks and
  deliveries under a private, owned, non-symlink root (0600 state, 0700 dir,
  local-store lock, atomic writes, fsync, 10k records / 16 MiB bounds; corrupt
  state is refused, never reset). Thread membership gates reads, posts and all
  task verbs; posts snapshot members so late joins never receive earlier
  messages. A task names one fleet item ID (unique board-wide); claim, renew,
  release and handoff validate the exact live `SharedStore` generation before
  mutating. Capability fields (ownerToken/ownerKey/queueId) never leave board
  state or CLI output. If the board write fails after a fleet mutation, the
  orphaned claimed lease stays fenced until expiry; nothing fabricates success
  or steals it back. `foundry.eventBus: false` refuses every verb before writes.
- `src/core/fleet/event-bus.ts`: new `bus:delivery` lifecycle event kind
  (frozen delivery payload), emitted best-effort after durable commit.
- `src/cli/fleet-bus.ts` (new): thin dispatcher for `phm bus thread|task` with
  strict arity, `--peer`, `--json`, `--root`, `--queue-root`, `--` literal
  handling, exit 0/1/2, and a fixed safe-error allowlist so private paths and
  filesystem errors never reach output. Honors `fleet.sharedQueue` filesystem
  mode (`path` + `trustedCoherentStorage: true`), then board at `<path>/bus`.
- Wiring: `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` (`bus` lazy entry),
  `src/cli/index.ts` (top-level `bus` delegates to fleet), `src/cli/completions.ts`
  (`bus` top-level + fleet verb + subcommands), `src/cli/help.ts` (help entry).
- Docs: `docs/BUS-THREADS.md` (usage, ownership, untrusted-content and storage
  contracts), index entries in `docs/README.md` and `docs/llms.txt`.
- Incidental fixes required for green checks: `src/cli/fleet-pr-repeats.ts`
  set the accepted-but-dead `--json` flag (pre-existing `prefer-const` lint
  error); `estates` and `ci-metrics` were dispatched in index.ts but missing
  from completions/help, failing `cli-registry-drift` on the base commit;
  entries added.

## Commands run

- `npm run install:worktree` (node_modules was incomplete; eslint/lib missing)
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/bus-board.test.ts` : 30/30 pass
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/cli-registry-drift.test.ts
  test/cli-completions-subcommands.test.ts test/completion-claims.test.ts

  test/fleet-verb-export-convention.test.ts test/fleet-verb-catalog-effect.test.ts
  test/fleet-registry-help.test.ts test/fleet-verb-registry-repair-01.test.ts
  test/fleet-verb-help-smoke.test.ts` : 699/699 pass
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/doc-facts.test.ts
  test/docs-llms-txt.test.ts test/docs-readme-links.test.ts
  test/docs-readme-packaged-links.test.ts test/documentation-navigation.test.ts
  test/docs-index-source-only-links.test.ts test/cli-help-exit.test.ts
  test/cli-help-no-side-effects.test.ts test/cli-help-safety-core.test.ts
  test/first-run-cli-help.test.ts test/m32.help.test.ts
  test/help-command-and-gateway-version.test.ts test/docs-fleet-verbs.test.ts
  test/fleet-verbs-cli.test.ts` : 1264/1264 pass
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/m241.event-bus.test.ts
  test/bus-envelope.test.ts test/bus-hoplog.test.ts test/bus-threads.test.ts
  test/m392.queue-lease-epochs.test.ts test/shared-queue-claim-lock-retry.test.ts`
  : all pass
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/m111.work-queue.test.ts
  test/m113.coordinator-wire.test.ts test/m114.shared-subscription.test.ts
  test/m220.anticlog-verdict-feedback.test.ts test/bus-inbox-oct31c.test.ts
  test/bus-inbox-expired-reclaim.test.ts` : all pass
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/authority-tier1-closure-310b.test.ts`
  : 4/4 pass (closure unchanged; event-bus imports bus-delivery as type only)
- `npm run typecheck` : pass (backend + web)

- `npm run check:docs` : pass, 0 errors

- New suite `test/bus-board.test.ts`: 30 pass, 0 fail (claim conflict, fleet

+1,120 (14 files: 9 modified, 5 new). No `.github/**` changes; no new tokens
or secrets; no em dashes in added lines; everything left uncommitted.

title: Fix authenticated Slack inbox receipts through the approved host writer
body:
Authenticated operator Slack requests could remain incomplete because the Leader network directly appended to an inbox intentionally protected by the host's sole-writer policy. Route Slack through that existing approved writer and require an exact request-bound durable receipt before advancing inbox or bus acceptance.

The host writer preserves legacy channel behavior and0444 restoration. New structured Slack records have fixed provenance, escaped body headings and full-byte duplicate reconciliation. Production invokes only the fixed helper with stdin-only text and a minimal environment, rechecking the current owner/approval and validating a closed receipt. Incomplete or uncertain outcomes remain retryable under the same request ID.

Validation:34 affected Leader/Slack cases,12 native helper cases and12 unchanged legacy cases pass; changed-file verification and canonical frontend TypeScript pass. Native tests use a source-owned approved scrubber fixture and prove operation with live host-state reads denied. Exact-capacity duplicate and forged/partial/conflicting receipt negatives pass.

This PR changes source only. Installing the reviewed host helper, adopting a qualified runtime and reconciling retained requests are separately coordinated. It grants no FDA, model execution permission or authority from message content.
